about.title: Calexico Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Calexico's mix of family-owned businesses, chain retailers near Rt 111, and residential complexes off Cole Road and Cesar Chavez means property owners have a duty to keep walkways, entrances, and parking areas reasonably safe. When they don't — a wet floor left unmarked, broken pavement, poor lighting in a stairwell — people get hurt. Because Calexico sits so close to the border, some falls happen at businesses with heavy foot traffic and quick turnover, which can make evidence disappear fast if no one documents it. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who understands how California premises liability law works and what it takes to build a claim. If you were injured because a property owner in Calexico failed to fix or warn about a hazard, reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of finding out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Reach Out After a Fall in Calexico

items.title: Notice Matters Under California Law
items.desc: You generally need to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. An independent attorney can help identify what evidence supports that.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Quickly
items.desc: Many Calexico businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting fast can make the difference between preserving proof of the hazard and losing it.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, though it can reduce what you receive. An attorney can help explain how shared fault might apply to your specific fall.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Calexico?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building near downtown Calexico, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. Speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later helps protect your options.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a store or apartment complex?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the hazard, note the time and location, and ask if there's a security camera nearby. Report the incident to a manager or property staff and request a copy of any written report. These steps help preserve evidence before conditions change or footage gets deleted.

items.question: Does it matter that Calexico is a smaller border city with fewer big retailers?
items.answer: Not really — the same California premises liability standards apply whether the fall happened at a large chain or a locally owned shop along Rt 111 or Cesar Chavez. What matters is whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An independent attorney can evaluate the property and circumstances regardless of the business's size.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We're not a law firm ourselves — we simply help connect you to someone who can evaluate your case.
